title: Ultraviolet exciton-polaritons in silver phenylthiolate
source: Matter
abstract: Hybridization of light and excitons can change how materials absorb and emit light, but achieving this in the ultraviolet remains challenging. We show that a layered silver phenylthiolate forms hybrid light-matter states in simple mirror structures. This material expands the options for controlling ultraviolet light and provides a foundation for exploring future light sources and light-driven chemistry.

title: Boundary density predicts catalyst-layer utilization in membrane-electrode assemblies
source: Joule
abstract: Catalyst layers in membrane-electrode assemblies are often underutilized, limiting the efficiency of electrochemical devices. This work identifies the mechanism that localizes reaction near the boundaries between contacted and non-contacted regions of the catalyst layer. Based on this insight, boundary density is introduced as a geometric descriptor of the porous-transport-layer/catalyst-layer interface and a predictor of catalyst-layer utilization.

title: 4f-multiplet-enabled electron–phonon decoupling towards high thermoelectric performance in rare-earth topological semimetal TbPtBi
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Topological materials exhibit strong magneto-thermoelectric effects owing to the ultrahigh mobility of electrons, yet bosonic phonon transport typically remains insensitive to magnetic fields. Crystal electric fields (CEF) combined with Zeeman splitting in rare-earth ions yielding discrete 4f excitation levels can in principle but have rarely been demonstrated to reduce phonon thermal conductivity by resonant phonon scattering. Therefore, rare-earth topological semimetals offer a unique platform in which electrical and phononic thermal transport can be intrinsically decoupled by magnetic fields. Herein, taking TbPtBi as an example, we demonstrate pronounced electron–phonon decoupling enabled by field-tunable 4f multiplets. High-mobility topological carriers give rise to high magneto-thermopowers and thermoelectric power factors. Meanwhile, multi-resonant phonon scattering by Zeeman-split Tb3+ CEF levels suppresses the phonon thermal conductivity, leading to a complete quenching of the phonon peak and a reduction of nearly 90% at 13 K by applying a magnetic field of ∼9 T. Theoretical calculations indicate a redistribution of phonon lifetimes that can drive the lattice into a phonon-glass-like state. These results establish 4f-multiplet engineering as a new way for electron-phonon decoupling and demonstrate the great potential of rare-earth topological materials for exceptional magneto-thermoelectric performance.

title: Conformational inversion mediated organic crystal actuator with extended stroke, self-healing, and optical switching
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Dynamic molecular crystals with the capability to effectively convert thermal energy into mechanical work offer a compelling platform for microactuators. However, developing crystalline actuation materials that simultaneously achieve large and reversible deformation, rapid response, robust cyclability, and integrated optoelectronic functionality remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we take advantage of the conformational inversion of cyclohexyl groups and have rationally developed a dynamic organic crystal based on a dibenzothiophene sulfone derivative, BcDT, which exhibits exceptionally large, rapid, and reversible elongation. The thermally induced chair-to-boat conformational inversion of the introduced cyclohexyl moieties drives a cooperative phase transition that yields a linear elongation of ~14.3% along the crystal long axis, which delivers a work density of ~6.8 × 102 J m−3 and an efficiency of ~0.014%. Notably, the crystal features an uncommon self-healing capability, autonomously repairing macroscopic cracks during heating/cooling stages, ensuring its structural integrity and reliable actuation over multiple thermal cycles. The phase transition also enables reversible switching of linear and nonlinear optical properties, including a 4.2-fold modulation of two-photon excited fluorescence and tunable polarization anisotropy. Leveraging these properties, we demonstrate that BcDT crystals can function as microactuator devices to propel a heavy object and cooperatively lift a platform. This work establishes a molecular design strategy that integrates rapid, high-stroke actuation, self-healing, and optical switching within a single crystalline system, overcoming key functional limitations of current microactuators based on dynamic molecular crystals.

title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documented pore’s charge and size, and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

title: Multiscale insights into zinc metal anodes for aqueous zinc ion batteries
source: Matter
abstract: This review examines how the intrinsic properties of zinc metal influence its stability in aqueous electrolytes, highlighting multiscale correlations among morphology, microstructure, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior. It outlines emerging strategies and future directions for enhancing zinc reversibility and utilization toward practical aqueous zinc ion batteries.

title: Beyond acceptor emissivity: interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder regulate nonradiative voltage losses for organic solar cells
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Suppressing non-radiative energy loss (ΔEnr) is critical for achieving high open-circuit voltage (VOC) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains unclear whether intrinsic emissive properties of acceptors can reliably predict voltage losses. Here, we report a counterintuitive phenomenon in which a low-emissive acceptor (D6) delivers a significantly reduced ΔEnr compared with the benchmark L8-BO when blended with D18. Despite lower intrinsic emissivity of D6, the D18: D6 system exhibits a markedly higher electroluminescence efficiency and a reduced ΔEnr of 0.153 eV, leading to an enhanced VOC of 0.980 V. Incorporation of D6 into the D18: L8-BO host yields a ternary device with a power conversion efficiency of 21.01%. Sensitive EQE analysis reveals that favorable CT-state energetics partially contribute to the reduced non-radiative loss of D18: D6, while temperature-dependent photoluminescence analysis further identifies suppressed interfacial dynamic disorder as a critical additional factor. While dynamic disorder is significantly increased in the D18: L8-BO blend, it is effectively suppressed in the D18: D6 system, resulting in preserved emissive interfacial states. Complementary structural and kinetic studies demonstrate that D6 modulates aggregation pathways and stabilizes nanoscale morphology, enabling efficient charge transport and reduced recombination. Furthermore, the beneficial role of D6 can be extended to multiple high-performance acceptor systems, demonstrating its general applicability as an interfacial regulator for improving photovoltaic performance. These results highlight that non-radiative voltage loss in OSCs is governed by the interplay between interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder rather than by the intrinsic emissivity of the acceptor alone, providing new insights into the design of low-energy-loss photovoltaic materials.

title: Back-end-of-line-integrated carbon nanotube modules for acceleration of silicon logic and clock networks
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Geometric transistor scaling no longer delivers proportional timing gains in advanced silicon logic integrated circuits (ICs), where operating frequency is increasingly bounded by high-capacitance, fanout-limited logic paths and clock networks. The emerging τ-scaling perspective reframes this limitation as a time-constant problem across the driver-interconnect-load system. Here we report τDrive, a monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) carbon-nanotube (CNT) active timing overlay that selectively compresses the dominant τ of silicon logic and clock paths. Unlike topology-folding approaches that primarily shorten interconnects, τDrive preserves the underlying silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) fabric and inserts back-end-of-line (BEOL) integrated CNT timing cells only at load-critical driver stages. A 180-nm Si/500-nm CNT experimental platform verifies low-temperature CNT-on-Si integration, and will enable CNT-assisted Si ring oscillators to achieve a 294% output-swing improvement and 30% effective-current enhancement with a fanout (FO) of 5. In simulations of a 3-nm Si central processing unit (CPU) using calibrated 10-nm CNT CMOS standard cells, selective CNT insertion reduces FO = 39 local delay and transition by 87.5% and 89.5%, respectively, and a single-cell replacement improves the full-CPU logic-path maximum frequency (Fmax) by 2.3%, while selective clock-tree enhancement raises the frequency bound from 2.85 to 2.93 GHz with only a 0.01 mW increase in clock-tree synthesis (CTS) power. These results establish CNT-on-Si M3D as a low-intrusion, vertically accessible drive resource for post-geometric τ compression, as well as a novel logic-folding approach.

title: Faster global mid-depth ocean connectivity in observations
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Ocean circulation redistributes heat, carbon, and biogeochemical tracers through transport pathways connecting distant ocean regions, yet global connectivity of mid-depth transport pathways remains poorly constrained by observations. Here we establish an observational benchmark of global mid-depth water-mass connectivity, using more than 1.3 million displacements recorded by 9,920 Argo floats over the past two decades. The benchmark reveals that observed connectivity is generally faster than simulated, with mean connectivity timescales 23-29% shorter in the real ocean. This systematic discrepancy between observed and simulated mid-depth ocean connectivity arises from overestimated turnover timescales within subtropical gyre interiors and underrepresentation of rapid inter-basin exchanges along equatorial and western boundary pathways in the simulation-derived networks, particularly in the South Pacific and South Atlantic. These findings provide quantitative constraints on ocean interior transport, with broad implications for estimates of climate memory, tracer age, carbon sequestration, and marine biogeographic connectivity.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO2, which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h−1, a high C2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g−1 h−1 and 90.1% C2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O2/CH4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C2H6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self‐repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial‐based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet‐adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid‐covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff‐base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine‐containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self‐healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host–graft integration, and cartilage‐like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet‐adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial–cartilage interface healing in fluid‐rich joint environments.

title: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10H‐Pyrido[1,2‐a]‐5‐indolium Salts
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Next‐generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent‐free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation‐caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion–π
                    +
                    interactions. Specifically, a rigid N‐doped fluorene (10
                    H
                    ‐pyrido[1,2‐
                    a
                    ]‐5‐indolium, PIn
                    +
                    ) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent‐free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

title: Rate Capability of Lithium‐Rich Manganese‐Based Oxide Cathodes: Charge–Discharge Kinetics, Multiscale Bottlenecks, and Dynamic Rate‐Determining Steps
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g
                    −1
                    through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast‐charging applications. This review deconstructs rate‐limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge‐transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate‐determining step (RDS) shifts from electron‐transfer to ion‐diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density (

Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often‐overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high‐rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross‐study C‐rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high‐rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.

title: Ion–Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single‐channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion‐electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual‐channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic‐light‐guided closed‐loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This “single device enabled, distinguishable dual‐channel readouts” principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

ABSTRACT

Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce

The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO

title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow‐loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, <16 µgIr cm
                    −
                    2
                    ) integrated within a hollandite MnO
                    2
                    framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm
                    −
                    2
                    from 580 mV (undoped α‐MnO
                    2
                    ) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrO
                    x
                    . Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP‐MS dissolution measurements with x‐ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH‐ and potential‐dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir‐efficient mixed‐metal oxide catalysts.

title: pH‐Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lipid membrane‐bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell‐like compartments for on‐demand biomolecule production. However, most cell‐free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user‐imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity‐transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex‐forming single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH‐responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger‐release pH, which is critical for enabling acid‐triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH‐responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity‐responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell‐penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target‐specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐value piezoelectric single‐crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor‐based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off‐cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling‐to‐device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg

A ball‐milling‐based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)‐assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi‐1–3‐like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single‐crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a

Comparative experiments and finite‐element simulations reveal that single‐crystal‐derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP‐induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm

title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non‐halogenated mixed‐solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS
                    2
                    ) and o‐xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high‐performance acceptor BTP‐eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat‐film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single‐crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II‐based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm
                    2
                    active area) fabricated by slot‐die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution‐processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single‐crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ‐Formed Ceramic–Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water‐rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm‐shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross‐linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual‐mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm
                    −
                    3
                    ) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame‐inhibiting SO
                    2
                    release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post‐test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO

                    3
                    to carbon. This trend in BO

                    fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high‐performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi‐stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next‐generation battery safety materials.

title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short‐Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed‐Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Conventional short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed‐dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier‐collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type‐II band‐aligned PTF/WSe

title: A Dual‐Locked and H2S‐NO Tandem‐Activatable NIR‐II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H
                    2
                    S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H
                    2
                    S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial‐ and Mesenchymal‐Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC‐Derived Intestinal Organoids
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill‐defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG‐ and Matrigel‐cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation‐associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM‐remodelling and integrin‐associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2‐positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

title: Skunk Cabbage‐Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Near‐infrared (NIR)‐responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade‐offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra‐fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR‐responsive actuators by integrating aggregation‐induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus‐structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra‐low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi‐donor‐π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions and molecular motion‐facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat‐transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

title: A heavy molybdenum reservoir in Neoarchean seawater tracks extensive iron oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The lead-up to the Great Oxidation Event (GOE; between 2.5 and 2.2 Ga) was arguably as consequential as the event itself, yet substantial uncertainties remain regarding the timing and magnitude of oxygen rise in early Earth’s oceans. Heavy molybdenum isotope compositions (δ
                    98
                    Mo) in Neoarchean marine sediments have traditionally been interpreted as evidence for adsorption of dissolved Mo onto iron oxyhydroxides [e.g., ferrihydrite; Fe(OH)
                    3
                    ] and manganese oxides (MnO
                    2
                    ) formed in oxygenated marine environments, implying at least regional surface oxygen accumulation immediately prior to the GOE. Here, we propose an alternate explanation in which these isotopic signatures arose in a largely anoxic ocean. Analyses of Neoarchean banded iron formations (BIFs) deposited at 2.57 to 2.51 Ga reveal a broad range of δ
                    98
                    Mo values, which are best explained by the combined effects of Mo adsorption onto primary ferrihydrite, followed by its diagenetic incorporation into Fe(II)-Mo(IV)-sulfides. After accounting for isotopic fractionation during adsorption, we estimate that Neoarchean seawater δ
                    98
                    Mo maintained a relatively stable composition between 1.5‰ and 1.6‰. A newly developed Mo isotope mass balance model further indicates that only a minor MnO
                    2
                    sink was required to generate these heavy δ
                    98
                    Mo values. Instead, the dominant control was likely removal of isotopically light Mo via adsorption to settling ferrihydrite particles in ferruginous seawater. Given the lack of oxygen indicators for cyanobacterial photosynthesis, we posit that anoxygenic photosynthetic bacteria (photoferrotrophs) were the primary drivers of ferrihydrite precipitation during BIF deposition. Together, these findings imply that the Neoarchean Mo isotope record reflects anaerobic biological oxidation of Fe(II) rather than pervasive surface seawater oxygenation preceding the GOE.

title: Extracellular vesicles presenting “don’t eat me” signal limit the efferocytic capacity in lung fibrosis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical “don’t eat me” mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically nonperturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to
                    elastic tricriticality
                    , characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd

Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

title: IFITM1-mediated restriction of henipavirus entry is associated with ephrinB2 reorganization and confinement in membrane nanodomains
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are prototype henipaviruses (HNV) within the family of
                    Paramyxoviridae
                    . They are highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxoviruses that cause fatal encephalitis in humans, with case fatality rates of 40 to 70%. These viruses use the receptor-binding protein (G) to engage host receptors ephrinB2 and/or ephrinB3, while the fusion protein (F) drives membrane fusion leading to virus entry and cell–cell fusion. Interferon-inducible transmembrane (IFITM) proteins restrict the infection of many unrelated viruses at virus entry. We show that the knockdown of IFITM1 enhances HNV entry and cell–cell fusion in both human epithelial and endothelial cells, while overexpression of IFITM1 inhibits both. Using single-molecule localization microscopy, we observed that IFITM1 forms nanoclusters on the plasma membrane that are enlarged upon interferon stimulation. IFITM1 clusters spatially co-occur with GM1-enriched, raft-like membrane domains. EphrinB2, a lipid raft resident, organizes into larger and denser clusters when associated with IFITM1, suggesting a preferential partitioning into membrane domains organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. Using single-particle tracking, we further show that lateral diffusion of ephrinB2 on the plasma membrane is confined in the presence of IFITM1. This confinement is not reversed by amphotericin B, nor is IFITM1-mediated NiV restriction. Our data show spatial reorganization and confinement of ephrinB2 within membrane domains that may be organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. These changes may contribute to HNV restriction, potentially by increasing the energy barrier for virus-cell membrane fusion and reducing productive virus-receptor encounters.

title: Homeostatic control of stem cell activity during intestinal regeneration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Stem cells proliferate rapidly to maintain tissue turnover during regeneration, yet the mechanisms preventing hyperproliferation remain unclear. Here, we identified nuclear factor Y (NF-Y) as a transcriptional repressor that maintains intestinal stem cell (ISC) quiescence. NF-Y restricts ISC proliferation by occupying the promoters of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling components, including
                    Egfr
                    ,
                    Mkp3
                    ,
                    Raf
                    ,
                    Ras
                    , and
                    pnt
                    , through regulation dependent on the histone acetyltransferase Nejire (Nej)/p300. Loss of NF-Y enhances ISC proliferation and accelerates tumor progression. NF-Y acts with Nej to restrict
                    Egfr
                    expression and suppress hyperproliferation. Together, these results demonstrate that NF-Y, acting with Nej, serves as a key transcriptional repressive brake that restrains growth-signaling to control stem cell activity under homeostatic and disease conditions.

title: Programmable multistable structures via bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Multistable structures, characterized by rapid shape morphing, instantaneous force amplification, and zero standby power, are pivotal for soft robotics and energy harvesting. However, achieving multistability while systematically controlling the accessible deformation modes remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a bioinspired, mechanically guided 4D printing approach to design and fabricate programmable multistable structures, including octastable and various bistable units, mimicking the growth-induced morphing of plant leaves and fruits. The stability landscapes of these units can be tuned by varying dimensionless geometric parameters and validated through buckling analysis. By integrating multiple octastable units, we demonstrate a compact, 10-cm-scale strip and a shape-morphing metasurface with configuration spaces of over one billion and four sextillion stable states. Furthermore, by modulating the dimensionless geometric parameters of multiunit structures, we identify a transition from bending to folding, enabling the creation of bistable hinges. As proof-of-concept demonstrations, we developed devices for directional droplet routing and mixing, reconfigurable electrical switching, conforming grasping of irregular objects, and programmable mechanical display. This work establishes a versatile framework for the design and fabrication of next-generation reconfigurable morphing systems and programmable flexible devices.

title: Host infection selects for sRNA variants that drive bacterial social cheating
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Single-nucleotide mutations in regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) represent a largely unexplored route to social cheating during bacterial infection. Here we show that
                    arcZ
                    , encoding a conserved Hfq-dependent sRNA in the plant pathogen
                    Dickeya solani
                    , undergoes recurrent single-nucleotide mutations during potato tuber infection. Five distinct
                    arcZ
                    alleles define a graded series of ArcZ functional impairment in which antifungal and protease activities are progressively reduced while virulence is compromised only in a subset of alleles. All five variants gain a fitness advantage exclusively during coinfection with wild-type
                    
                      arcZ
                      1
                    
                    cells. This advantage is strongest when variants are rare and declines as cheater frequency increases, ultimately correlating with reduced total bacterial productivity, the canonical signature of social cheating and a tragedy of the commons. No fitness benefit is detected
                    in vitro
                    . Transcriptomic profiling of five
                    arcZ
                    variants identifies a conserved core of 186 downregulated genes enriched in secreted and diffusible functions. Systematic genetic dissection, supported by quantitative proteomics, establishes BudAB-dependent limitation of tissue acidification as the dominant cooperative public good exploited during infection. Wild-type
                    
                      arcZ
                      1
                    
                    cells divert pyruvate flux toward acetoin via the BudAB pathway, maintaining a less acidic tissue environment that sustains disease progression;
                    arcZ
                    variants, which show reduced expression of this pathway, benefit from the less acidic environment maintained by wild-type cells without contributing to it. These results establish pleiotropic regulatory sRNAs as a previously unrecognized class of mutational targets for the emergence of social cheaters during host infection.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell–cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8–DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s’ C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8–Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8’s ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock, upregulated HspA6 and HspA8 then limit the HSR presumably targeted by heat-induced DnaJB1. HspA6 knock-down and overproduction in HeLa cells suggest that HspA6 functions in preventing an overshoot of the HSR.

title: RNA and proteins joined up at the origins of life: Persistence is the point
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: What drove nucleic acids (NA) into functional associations with proteins (PR) at the origins of life? We reason from polymer physics and the Central Dogma that the fitness value of cooperating through a division of labor—NA for replication fidelity and PR for functional fitness—is much higher than for either polymer alone. Our model shows a Pareto Front, where NA and PR can bootstrap each other to achieve autocatalytic cooperativity toward biology.

title: VAMP725 and VAMP726 interact with cellulose synthase to support secondary cell wall formation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The formation of plant cell walls underpins morphogenesis, growth, and development of all plants. Cellulose is an essential and load-bearing cell wall polymer that is synthesized by Cellulose Synthase (CESA) protein complexes at the plasma membrane. In this study, we reveal that SNARE proteins Vesicle Associated Membrane Protein 726 (VAMP726) and VAMP725 associate with multiple CESA proteins. Consistent with these results, the VAMP726 is codelivered with the CESA proteins to the plasma membrane, and the proteins colocalize at intracellular compartments. We further show that the VAMPs, especially VAMP726, are important for CESA trafficking and sustenance of cellulose synthesis both in growing tissues and in secondary wall producing maturing tissues. Taken together, our study outlines an important intracellular process whereby VAMP proteins facilitate trafficking of CESA complexes during cellulose synthesis.

title: Stereodynamical control of a four-atom reaction: HD + OH → D + H2O
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
To date, studies of differential steric effect in reactive collisions have been limited to atom + molecule systems. How stereodynamics is affected when the other reactant is also a molecule remains an open question. Here, we present a combined high-resolution crossed-beam scattering and full-dimensional quantum dynamical study of the HD (

                    = 1,
                    j
                    = 2) + OH → D + H

                    O reaction, in which the HD molecular axis was initially prepared either parallel or perpendicular to the relative velocity using the stimulated Raman pumping scheme. The OH reactant was unpolarized and in its ground vibrational state, with a rotational temperature of ~85 K in the experiment, and was restricted to the ground rovibrational state in the theory. Pronounced stereodynamic effects are observed in both the backward scattering intensity and the product angular distributions. Detailed analysis of scattering wavefunctions reveals that the initial
                    m
                    = ±2 states access a noncoplanar dynamical transition state, distinct from that accessed by
                    m
                    = 0 (
                    m
                    denotes the projection of
                    j
                    along the direction of relative velocity). The nonzero dihedral angle, a geometric degree of freedom absent in triatomic reactions, leads to reduced reactivity and enhances sideward scattering for the perpendicular configuration, while leaving the product rovibrational state distributions essentially unchanged. In addition, the alignment of the HD rotational angular momentum is preserved in the rotational direction of the product H
                    2
                    O.

title: A trefoil knot mimic and multiple pore states define the mechanism of a split-shell Tc toxin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Toxin complex (Tc) toxins are among the largest virulence factors secreted by pathogenic bacteria, operating via a sophisticated injection mechanism that translocates cytotoxic effectors into host cells. While most structural and mechanistic studies have focused on fused-shell Tc toxins such as PTC3 from
                    Photorhabdus luminescens
                    , the structurally distinct split-shell toxins remain poorly understood. Here we report cryoelectron microscopy structures of the split-shell
                    Yersinia entomophaga
                    Tc holotoxin (YenTc) in multiple conformational states at resolutions of 2.6 to 3.7 Å. We show that the chitinase subunit YenChi2 is essential for shell expression and stabilizes the N terminus of the shell subunit YenA1 in the prepore state. Our structures also reveal the first trefoil knot mimic in Tc toxins, which serves the dual function of stabilizing the linker domain and holding the two halves of the split shell together. We further describe three distinct pore states: the conventional pore state, an inverted pore state in which the shell rotates 180° around a hinge in YenA2, and a lollipop pore state induced at alkaline pH in which the YenA1-YenChi2 subcomplex fully dissociates from the channel. Strikingly, all three pore states also manifest in the TcA pentamer of
                    P. luminescens
                    PTC3, indicating that they represent a general but previously undescribed feature of Tc toxin pore formation. Taken together, our results establish a mechanistic framework for split-shell Tc toxins and expose a dynamic, multilevel intoxication pathway that may apply broadly to Tc toxins.

title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito
                    Anopheles gambiae
                    , reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore–lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

title: Acute degradation of Pumilio proteins reveals a biphasic posttranscriptional regulatory hierarchy in embryonic stem cell fate decision
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Posttranscriptional regulation is critical for mammalian embryogenesis yet has been underexplored. We previously showed that RNA-binding Pumilio proteins (Pum1/2) are essential for early mouse embryogenesis and embryonic stem cell (ESC) functions. Here, using acute protein degradation systems combined with time-resolved RNA sequencing and enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation, we delineate a two-phase regulatory hierarchy modulated by Pum1/2 in mouse ESCs. The first phase, occurring within 10 h of Pum1/2 depletion, is predominantly stabilization of over 100 Pum1/2-target mRNAs, while the second phase, occurring in subsequent 66 h, propagates to over 1,000 mRNAs mostly through indirect regulatory effects. Functionally, Pum1/2 depletion delays transition from naïve to formative pluripotency and alters expression trajectories of neuroectoderm and germline genes during early differentiation. Mechanistically, Pum1/2 directly repress mRNAs encoding Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 subunits, including
                    Suz12
                    , thereby potentially constraining H3K27me3 deposition at neuroectodermal gene loci. These findings establish Pum1/2 as biphasic posttranscriptional regulators of pluripotency and lineage balance.

title: Determining Composition–Structure–Property Relationships in Quaternary Perovskitoids Through Megalibraries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Understanding how composition governs structure and function is essential for designing functional materials, however, establishing these relationships remains prohibitively slow for materials with massive and tunable compositional spaces, such as Bi and Sb‐based perovskitoids. Here, a novel megalibrary‐based synthetic methodology has been developed and used to rapidly identify and characterize quaternary perovskite derivatives across an expansive compositional space. Parylene templates were used to synthesize one million compositionally distinct, positionally encoded Cs
                    3
                    Sb
                    2−x
                    Bi
                    x
                    Br
                    9−y
                    I
                    y
                    microcrystals on 2 × 2 cm
                    2
                    chips with 20 µm periodicity. These megalibraries enabled the systematic investigation of structural and optoelectronic evolution across this compositional space using micro‐area x‐ray diffraction, position‐resolved absorbance spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and confocal fluorescence microscopy. An unusual non‐monotonic bandgap shift was observed with increasing Br content, reaching a minimum at 33% Br. This behavior is attributed to the formation of halide‐segregated heterostructures, consisting of low‐dimensional, I‐rich shells surrounding Br‐rich layered cores. Phase separation was most pronounced in Sb‐rich compositions, which were found to stabilize heterostructure formation. This study demonstrates how megalibraries enable the simultaneous evaluation of key optoelectronic parameters, including bandgap and phase purity, revealing complex, composition‐dependent structure‐function relationships in perovskitoids and providing a versatile platform for accelerating the discovery of optoelectronic‐relevant materials.

title: Frontispiece: Diverting Reaction Pathways: Shunt Catalysis for Robust C═O Hydrogenation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: In the Research Article e3975660, Xinping Duan, Youzhu Yuan, and co-workers report that the “catalytic shunt” strategy awakens thermodynamically stable yet kinetically inert interfaces by spatially segregating H2 activation and dimethyl oxalate (DMO) adsorption. The unique Ag/CeO2||SiO2 configuration, activated hydrogen spills over from Ag/SiO2 to hydrogenate pre-polarized DMO on Ag/CeO2, achieving a 6-fold turnover frequency boost and >1000-hour stability for methyl glycolate.

title: Intrinsically Stretchable Fully π‐Conjugated Polymer Films Enabled by Supramolecular Plasticized Micro‐Crosslinking‐Network for Flexible Polymer Light‐Emitting Diodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stretchable fully π‐conjugated polymers (FπCPs) films with a fantastic optoelectronic property and outstanding deformation tolerance capacity, is a promising candidate for the fabrication of flexible optoelectronics devices. However, previous reported stretchable FπCPs films undergo irreversible chain slippage and alignment upon strain release, leading to plastic deformation, and consequently severe performance degradation during cyclic‐deformation operation. Herein, we proposed a supramolecular soft‐micro‐crosslinked strategy to achieve the stretchable
                    p
                    ‐
                    n
                    FπCPs (P
                    X
                    ‐OXI
                    1‐X
                    ‐HDI) films with a recoverable‐deformation ability for the flexible electronics. Three‐dimensional (3D) supramolecular micro‐crosslinked network formed by oxime‐urethane and hydrogen bonds allow for the excellent elastic deformation to dissipate transient stress while fundamentally suppressing permanent chain slippage. Micro‐crosslinked
                    p
                    ‐
                    n
                    FπCPs free‐standing films achieved an elongation at break of > 40%. Flexible PLED based on P
                    X
                    ‐OXI
                    1‐X
                    ‐HDI showed a stable green emission with brightness of ∼3300 cd cm
                    −2
                    . Meanwhile, the performance of transferred PLED based on stretchable micro‐crosslinked films are independent on the tensile ratio (>20%) with a maximum brightness of ∼2000 cd m
                    −2
                    , revealed the excellent cycle‐deformation‐stability than device based on crosslinked films. Therefore, these supramolecular micro‐crosslinked networks can enhance instantaneous toughness and confer a critical resistance to long‐term stress relaxation and plastic deformation, further ensure the device excellent deformation stability.

title: Polymer‐Directed Crystal Growth Regulation: Template‐Free Synthesis of Mesoporous Single‐Crystalline Mn2OBO3
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Transition metal borates are attractive anode candidates for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) because of their high specific capacity and environmental benignity; however, their structural collapse induced by large volume changes during cycling leads to rapid capacity degradation. In this study, we report a polymer‐directed crystal growth regulation strategy that enables the template‐free synthesis of mesoporous single‐crystalline Mn
                    2
                    OBO
                    3
                    (MSC Mn
                    2
                    OBO
                    3
                    ). Polyethyleneimine (PEI) acts as a bifunctional regulator, coordinating Mn
                    2+
                    ions and hydrogen bonding with borate ions to modulate hydrolysis and condensation, thereby yielding a hybrid precursor. Subsequent hydrothermal treatment yields single‐crystalline MnBO
                    2
                    OH nanobelts, which are converted by calcination into MSC Mn
                    2
                    OBO
                    3
                    . As an anode active material for lithium‐ion batteries, MSC Mn
                    2
                    OBO
                    3
                    delivers a reversible capacity of 1440 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.2 A g
                    −1
                    , more than twice that of bulk Mn
                    2
                    OBO

                    . Notably, this polymer‐directed strategy is readily extendable to doped MSC Mn

                    (e.g., Fe, V, and Mg), providing a versatile platform for the design of porous single‐crystalline materials for energy storage.

title: Efficient H2O2 Photosynthesis With Valorization by X‐Packing NDI Cocrystal Catalyst
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solar‐driven photocatalytic H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    synthesis offers a sustainable and green alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. However, coordinated regulation of electron‐transfer (ET) and energy‐transfer (EnT) pathways for efficient H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production remains challenging. Organic charge‐transfer (CT) cocrystals, which reconfigure the energy‐level structure through new intermolecular electronic states, provide a promising avenue to overcome this limitation. Herein, we report a CT cocrystal photocatalyst, DPNDI‐Py, prepared by liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) of N, N′‐bis(4‐pyridyl)‐1,4,5,8‐naphthalenediimide (DPNDI) and pyrene (Py). The cocrystal harbors an X‐packed donor‐acceptor arrangement, with a crossing angle of 52° between the long axes of DPNDI and Py. Spectroscopic measurements confirm strong intermolecular CT, and transient spectroscopy supports CT‐related excited‐state dynamics and the formation of long‐lived triplet states, while theoretical calculations indicate electronic structure favorable for intersystem crossing (ISC). Mechanistic studies indicate that both EnT and ET pathways are utilized in photocatalysis. Under LED irradiation in air, DPNDI‐Py delivers an average H

                    production rate of 18.47 ± 0.57 mmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    coupled with an 83.7 ± 2.26% dehydroascorbic acid (DHA) yield from ascorbic acid (AA) oxidation. This work provides mechanistic insight into CT‐mediated photocatalysis, offering a design principle for organic photocatalysts.

title: Dual Metal Dopants Advance Near‐Room‐Temperature PbS‐based Thermoelectrics
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title: Nonlinear Kinetic Optimization via Strong–Weak Cosolvent Synergy in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cosolvent engineering for aqueous Zn metal batteries has traditionally emphasized thermodynamic stabilization, whereas the kinetic dimension of Zn
                    2+
                    charge transfer—particularly in multi‐cosolvent systems—remains far less understood. Here we conduct a systematic study on a dual‐cosolvent electrolyte pairing a strong cosolvent (DMSO) with a weak cosolvent (DMC). Through spatial decoupling, the strong cosolvent directly coordinates to stabilize the primary solvation shell, while the weak cosolvent forms a dynamic outer‐shell buffer. This unique context modulates Zn–ligand binding, facilitates desolvation, and guides the formation of a regulated SEI. Consequently, this architecture preserves comparably high thermodynamic stability while unlocking a nonlinear kinetic optimization exclusive to the dual‐cosolvent regime. Using a multi‐descriptor framework, we demonstrate a ∼40% reduction in the charge‐transfer barrier relative to single‐cosolvent systems. This kinetic enhancement translates into robust practical performance, establishing strong–weak cosolvent synergy as a versatile design principle for next‐generation aqueous batteries.

title: Lumped Circuits Modeling of Dynamic Energy Transfer in Triboelectric Nanogenerators with Nonlinear Electromechanical Coupling
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Powering autonomous electronics, sensors, and wearable systems using small‐scale daily mechanical energy is becoming increasingly important. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a lightweight, flexible, and adaptable route for such applications, particularly when movements are involved. Here, we present a first‐of‐its‐kind unified dynamic energy‐transfer framework for TENGs, coupling their mechanical and electrical domains through a lumped element‐based equivalent circuit (LEEC) model. The framework captures time‐varying electrostatic behavior and key mechanical parameters, mass, damping, and stiffness, within a single predictive platform, enabling system‐level analysis of dynamic efficiency, impedance, resonance, and power transfer under different excitation conditions. The Thévenin equivalent model reveals that TENG performance is dynamically governed by excitation frequency, resonance, load matching, and surface charge density, approaching a time‐averaged theoretical efficiency of ∼54%. Experimental validation across devices with varied mechanical parameters shows close agreement with theory in electrical response and frequency‐dependent behavior. Furthermore, four borophene‐modified TENGs with different charge‐generation characteristics exhibit a systematic increase in electrical output and an estimated efficiency of up to 14.2% for the examined parameter space, supporting the model‐predicted dependence of energy‐conversion performance on surface charge density. The LEEC‐guided platform enables coupled energy and information harvesting through resonance‐enhanced capacitor charging and self‐powered road‐state sensing.

title: Characterizing Fill Factor Limitations in Perovskite‐Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Monolithic perovskite‐silicon tandem solar cells have achieved power conversion efficiencies approaching 35%. However, a significant gap remains to their thermodynamic limit, primarily due to fill factor (
                    FF
                    ) losses. This work presents a methodology to identify the underlying mechanisms of the losses. Electroluminescence characterization reveals the potential
                    FF
                    without series resistance losses but cannot fully explain the observed
                    FF
                    limitations. An additional loss mechanism is the photoshunt, a phenomenon which the parallel shunt resistance apparently reduces under illumination in perovskite solar cells. Using an analytical model, we show that the photoshunt originates from competition between charge extraction, governed by transport‐layer properties and electric field, and recombination in the absorber and at interfaces. An equivalent circuit model quantifies its impact on subcell and tandem
                    FF
                    . Additionally, the two‐diode property of the Si subcell can also influence the tandem
                    FF
                    losses. Measurements on tandem devices under spectrally independent LED illumination show that photoshunt losses can be hidden under bottom‐cell‐limited conditions, explaining the preference for slightly bottom‐cell‐limited tandem designs. Reducing the photoshunt through improved charge transport and reduced recombination could enable operation closer to current matching while minimizing
                    FF
                    and efficiency losses.

title: Synergistic Surface‐Bulk Induction of Uniform Out‐of‐Plane (100) Orientation for High‐Efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Perovskite thin films featuring out‐of‐plane oriented (100) crystallographic facets are pivotal for advancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells, owing to their superior charge transport properties and reduced deep‐level defect density. However, conventional single‐strategy modification approaches are typically constrained by limited control over crystal orientation and spatially heterogeneous orientation distribution, hindering the full exploitation of such beneficial facets. Herein, we present a surface‐bulk synergistic induction strategy that overcomes the limitations of single modification approaches, effectively promoting directional grain alignment and cooperatively guiding ordered out‐of‐plane growth during thermal annealing. Benefiting from the successful fabrication of a perovskite film with a uniform and predominant preferred orientation, the inverted perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.98% (certified 26.41%). Furthermore, the homogeneous texture and high intrinsic stability of the (100) facets enable the devices to retain 93.5% of their initial PCE after 1000 h of operational stability testing. This strategy effectively tackles the technical constraints of precursor solution regulation and solid‐state surface treatment, offering a novel research model for the precise modulation of perovskite thin film crystal facets and the secondary growth of polycrystalline thin films.
